title: adjudication batch output (NNN.out.json)
description: The contract between `entity-adjudicator` and `brain resolve merge-decisions`. One decision per pair in the matching .in.json — no more, no fewer. Two rules this file cannot check are enforced by merge-decisions and reject the whole batch: every `pair_id` must be one of the pairs in that input, and every pair must be answered. Only `same` merges; `different` and `unsure` are recorded and change nothing.

batch_id.description: Exactly the `batch_id` of the .in.json this answers, e.g. "shard-01/003".

decisions.description: One entry per pair in the input, in any order.

notes.description: Free-text remarks for the report — something the three verdicts cannot express. Never a place to hide a pair you could not judge: that pair gets `unsure`.

pair_id.description: Copied exactly from the pair in the .in.json. 16 hex characters.

verdict.description: `same` = one real-world thing under two names, and the evidence says so. `different` = the evidence says they are two things. `unsure` = the evidence does not decide; it is a good answer, and it merges nothing. A wrong `same` deletes a node and cannot be undone from inside the graph.

reason.description: One sentence naming the deciding evidence — the shared item, the conflicting role, the timeline. Not "the names look alike": that is what put the pair in front of you.
